text:
maria: Heads-up — compliance asked us to shorten the raw SIEM export retention window for tenant-scoped forensic snapshots. They want default raw retention 7 days, with a short, auditable JIT path to extend to 90 days for approved incidents. How do folks feel about a timeboxed encrypted snapshot + playback-only viewer approach?

kevin: agree with timeboxing. my concern is build complexity for the JIT unwrap flow and ensuring we don't break current runbooks. can we reuse the existing KMS proxy we have for ephemeral downloads?

aj: re: runbooks — if we change defaults we need oncall triggers, SLO rollback options, and alerting when any snapshot is extended. also need a clear TTL metric in the console.

sec-bot: Policy doc uploaded: https://redwood.internal/docs/sec/forensic-window-slimming.md :thumbsup:

natalie: from compliance: 7d default is our ask, but must have chain-of-custody logs for any 90d extension. extension requests need approver + business justification + ticket id. auto-approve only for legal holds.

maria: thanks. proposal: store snapshots encrypted-at-rest with CMK. default S3 lifecycle DELETE after 7d. when an incident owner requests extension, create an audit ticket, grant a timeboxed grant via KMS proxy (unwrap token valid N hours), and copy the snapshot to an "extended-forensics" bucket with a retention tag until 90d. all moves are logged.

kevin: implementation sketch — use S3 object tags + lifecycle rules and a small Lambda that handles the extension workflow. Lambda calls KMS:GenerateDataKey for the copy, writes audit event to sqs->observability. snippet: 
```bash
# pseudo-workflow
aws s3 cp s3://forensic-snapshots/$OBJ ./tmp && \
aws s3 cp ./tmp s3://extended-forensics/$OBJ --tagging "retention=90d;ticket=$TICKET"
# KMS proxy only issues plaintext key to Lambda and only for N hours
```

aj: can we avoid copying raw data between buckets? that's extra cost. maybe make an access wrapper that proxies reads against original bucket but enforces tag+ticket check and emits the same audit events.

maria: good point. wrapper-proxy is nicer. tradeoff: must ensure the original lifecycle doesn't delete during the extended period — so the workflow would still need to set a hold tag on the object before the grant is given. the hold tag can be removed when extension expires.

natalie: also require that any playback viewer is read-only and redacts PII by default. if forensics needs raw, that must be justified and logged via the ticket.

oncall-desk: ops note: make sure the canary test for deletion TTL is updated. we had a bug last quarter where lifecycle ran a day early. :grimacing:

kevin: agree. I'll prototype proxy + tag-hold approach. rough ETA: spike next week. i'll post a design doc and a small sequence diagram.

maria: thanks. items for follow-up: (1) kevin to spike proxy + tag-hold, (2) aj to update runbook alerts and rollback, (3) natalie to finalize approver matrix for 90d requests, (4) sec-bot to link updated playbook in docs. deadline: sync in eng-security on Wed.
